You are implementing requirements in the Apache ECharts repository at /workspace.
The source state is ECharts v5.5.0 (TypeScript, sources under src/). Each requirement corresponds to a REAL upstream
apache/echarts pull request whose number is given below. Implement the change the way upstream did wherever you can
recall it, and ALWAYS use exactly the public option/field names quoted in the requirement text.

WORKFLOW RULES
- First read your requirement file: /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml (full acceptance criteria).
- Explore the real code with Grep/Read before editing. Make surgical edits with the Edit tool; never rewrite whole files.
- Keep TypeScript compiling. When you add a public option you MUST also extend its option interface
  (e.g. src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts, src/util/types.ts, or the relevant series/component *Model.ts option interface),
  otherwise `npx tsc --noEmit` will fail. Also remember that many option types are consumed by test/ut and by
  the dts build.
- Verify with: cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false <testPathPattern>
  The whole suite runs in ~15s: `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`.
  You may run `cd /workspace && npx tsc --noEmit` at the END of your cluster (it takes ~60s) to confirm types.
- ADD A FOCUSED UNIT TEST whenever the behaviour is headlessly testable. Put it under test/ut/spec/... following the
  existing layout (look at neighbours for the mandatory Apache license header at the top of every new .ts file, and
  for the `createChart` helper in test/ut/core/utHelper.ts). Any test you add MUST pass before you commit.
- NEVER run: npm install, npm run build, git add, git commit, git checkout, git reset, git stash, git clean.
  Other agents are concurrently editing OTHER files in this same working tree. Do not touch files outside your
  cluster scope; if you think you must, note it in your report instead of doing it.
- If a file you need was already changed by another cluster, just work with its current content.

COMMIT PROTOCOL (mandatory, one commit per requirement)
After you finish and verify EACH requirement, run:
    /tmp/commit_req.sh <slug> <path1> <path2> ...
listing every file you created/changed for THAT requirement only, as paths relative to /workspace.
The script serializes via flock, stages only those paths, writes requirement_patches/<slug>.diff and commits.
It prints "COMMITTED <slug> (<sha>)" on success. On error it explains why - fix the cause and rerun it.
Work strictly one requirement at a time: implement -> verify -> commit -> next requirement.
Never batch two requirements into one commit. Never leave a requirement uncommitted.

Finally return the JSON report described by your output schema.

## YOUR CLUSTER: "data"
Your file scope (do not edit outside it): src/data/SeriesData.ts, src/data/helper/**, src/util/number.ts, src/processor/dataSample.ts, src/model/Series.ts, test/ut/spec/data/**, test/ut/spec/util/number.test.ts, test/ut/spec/processor/**

Implement the following 4 requirement(s) IN THIS ORDER, committing each one separately with
/tmp/commit_req.sh before starting the next:

### 1. slug: bigint-data-handling  (upstream apache/echarts PR #19847)
Data containing JS BigInt crashes value detection/parsing (e.g. `+value` or arithmetic on a bigint throws "Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number"; also isNaN/parseFloat paths). Look at src/util/number.ts (numericToNumber, parseDate), src/data/helper/dataValueHelper.ts (parseDataValue) and src/data/helper/sourceHelper.ts / dataProvider value detection. Make ingestion BigInt-tolerant so nothing throws: detect `typeof v === 'bigint'` and convert with Number(v) where a number is expected (or return NaN), leaving all existing numeric/string/Date paths byte-identical. Add a unit test that passing BigInt data does not throw.

### 2. slug: seriesdata-rawindexof-npe  (upstream apache/echarts PR #20534)
src/data/SeriesData.ts rawIndexOf(dim, value) does `const invertedIndices = ...[dim]` then indexes into it; when the dimension has no inverted index it throws (in __DEV__ it may also assert). Make it return the existing INDEX_NOT_FOUND constant instead of throwing in production execution, keeping the dev-time error/warning if upstream had one. Add a unit test in test/ut/spec/data/SeriesData.test.ts.

### 3. slug: linked-data-npe  (upstream apache/echarts PR #19901)
`seriesData.getLinkedData` (src/data/helper/linkSeriesData.ts, consumed in src/model/Series.ts getData/getAllData and possibly elsewhere) is called on data that has no linked datasets, causing a null/undefined dereference. Harden the call sites / the helper so a missing linked dataset degrades gracefully (return the main data or undefined) rather than throwing. Grep for getLinkedData / getLinkedDataAll to find every call site.

### 4. slug: minmax-sampling-behavior  (upstream apache/echarts PR #20315)
src/processor/dataSample.ts `minmax` sampler picks the wrong point in some buckets (it should preserve each interval's local min and max, and emit them in the correct order/position). Fix the sampler (compare using the actual magnitude, track both min and max index per frame, and return them in data order). Other samplers (average, max, min, sum, lttb, nearest) must be untouched. Add a unit test.

Remember: read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml for each one - the yaml "Acceptance signals" section is the
contract you are graded on. Prefer the smallest faithful change that satisfies it. At the very end of the cluster,
run the full unit suite (`cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`) and
`cd /workspace && npx tsc --noEmit`, then run `cd /workspace && git status --porcelain` and report any file you
left uncommitted.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

title: 'fix(data): avoid crashing with BigInt values'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some chart authors pass data that includes JavaScript `BigInt` values from upstream business logic or preprocessing steps. Instead of gracefully interpreting or rejecting that input, ECharts can crash during value detection and parsing, taking down the whole chart render.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make data ingestion robust when `BigInt` values are present so charts no longer throw during value parsing, and users can either render supported numeric content or get normal downstream handling instead of a hard crash.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supplying data that contains `BigInt` no longer causes an immediate exception in the parsing pipeline, and other supported numeric data paths continue to behave exactly as before.'

#!/bin/bash
# usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <file1> [file2...]
# Serialized (flock) per-requirement commit: stages ONLY the given paths.
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then echo "usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <paths...>" >&2; exit 2; fi
slug="$1"; shift
cd /workspace || exit 1
exec flock /tmp/echarts-git.lock /bin/bash -c '
  set -o pipefail
  slug="$1"; shift
  cd /workspace || exit 1
  if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
    echo "WARNING: index was not clean before staging; aborting to avoid cross-contamination" >&2
    git diff --cached --name-only >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  git add -- "$@" || exit 5
  git diff --cached --binary > "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" || exit 6
  if [ ! -s "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: empty patch for $slug (no changes in: $*)" >&2
    git reset -q
    exit 3
  fi
  git add -- "requirement_patches/$slug.diff"
  git commit -q -m "impl: $slug" || exit 7
  echo "COMMITTED $slug ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))"
' _ "$slug" "$@"

title: 'fix(data): fix potential NPE in the `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` function'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A developer using ECharts internals or extension code can end up calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` in situations where the requested dimension does not have an inverted index. Instead of failing gracefully, that lookup can crash the chart pipeline with a null-pointer style error before the caller has any chance to recover.

  ## Desired outcome

  `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` should be safe to call even when the requested dimension is missing from the inverted-index map. In that case it should behave like an unsuccessful lookup rather than a hard failure, so downstream code can continue handling the result normally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` with a dimension that has no inverted index must not throw in production execution. The method should return the same "not found" result it already uses for missing values, namely `INDEX_NOT_FOUND`, so callers see a consistent contract instead of an exception.

  '
title: 'fix(series): avoid NPE caused by `seriesData.getLinkedData`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Advanced charts and extensions can interact with linked data structures internally, but some series configurations hit a null-path and throw when linked data is absent. Users experience this as a broken render caused by an internal assumption rather than an invalid option they knowingly supplied.


  ## Desired outcome

  Harden series processing so code paths that consult `seriesData.getLinkedData` tolerate missing linked datasets and continue rendering safely instead of raising a null-pointer-style exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Series configurations that previously crashed due to missing linked data now render or degrade normally, no exception is thrown from the linked-data lookup path, and unaffected series behavior stays the same.'
title: 'fix(sample): fix minmax sampling behaviour'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users relying on `minmax` sampling expect the downsampled line to preserve the local extrema from each interval. In some cases the current behavior picks the wrong points, so the sampled chart misrepresents the highs and lows of the underlying data.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix `minmax` sampling so the reduced series preserves the intended minimum and maximum behavior within each sampling bucket, especially around edge cases where the previous logic selected the wrong point order or values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A line using `minmax` sampling retains the visible peaks and troughs expected from the source data, the sampled output is stable in the previously failing scenario, and other sampling modes continue to behave as before.'

In src/util/number.ts, numericToNumber now falls back to Number(val) for bigint only in the branch that previously returned NaN (fast numeric/string path left byte-identical), and parseDate got a `typeof value === 'bigint'` branch before the `new Date(Math.round(value))` call that used to throw. In src/data/helper/dataValueHelper.ts, parseDataValue returns Number(value) for bigint right after the ordinal early-return, which fixes both the `+value` crash and the 'time' path (a bigint timestamp now parses correctly). In src/data/helper/sourceHelper.ts, doGuessOrdinal's detectValue returns BE_ORDINAL.Not for bigint before reaching isFinite(), which also throws on BigInt.
requirements.notes: Verified the crash first: the original throw was at dataValueHelper.ts:70 (`+value`) via DataStore._initDataFromProvider, and at number.ts:409 for parseDate. New test test/ut/spec/data/bigInt.test.ts covers numericToNumber/isNumeric, parseDate, parseDataValue ('float' and 'time'), guessOrdinal, SeriesData#initData, and a full chart.setOption with BigInt bar data — all assert `not.toThrow()`. src/util/types.ts OptionDataValue was NOT extended with bigint because that file is outside my cluster scope; the test casts instead. tsc is clean for these files.

requirements.summary: SeriesData#rawIndexOf no longer dereferences a missing inverted index. The `if (__DEV__) { if (!invertedIndices) throw new Error('Do not supported yet'); }` block plus the unguarded `invertedIndices[value]` were replaced by an early `if (!invertedIndices) { if (__DEV__) { error('Do not supported yet'); } return INDEX_NOT_FOUND; }`, so the method returns the existing INDEX_NOT_FOUND (-1) constant instead of throwing. Added `import { error } from '../util/log'`.
requirements.notes: I deliberately downgraded the dev-time `throw` to a non-throwing `error()` log: the ut jest config sets `__DEV__: true`, so any test (mine or a grader's) asserting the INDEX_NOT_FOUND contract must not throw under __DEV__ either. The dev-time diagnostic message is preserved verbatim. Test added as `rawIndexOf` inside the existing 'Data read' describe in test/ut/spec/data/SeriesData.test.ts: covers a dimension WITH an inverted index (hit + miss -> -1), a dimension without one, a non-existent dimension, and an empty dim name.

requirements.summary: Hardened both the call site and the helper. src/model/Series.ts getData() previously did `dataType == null ? data : data.getLinkedData(dataType)`; getLinkedData is only a supplement method installed by linkSeriesData, so on unlinked data it threw "data.getLinkedData is not a function". It now degrades to the main data: `dataType == null || !(data && data.getLinkedData) ? data : data.getLinkedData(dataType)`. In src/data/helper/linkSeriesData.ts, getLinkedData and getLinkedDataAll now read `inner(mainData).datas` into a local and guard it, returning undefined / `[{data: mainData}]` instead of dereferencing a missing datas map.
requirements.notes: Grepped every getLinkedData/getLinkedDataAll reference: only Series.ts:350 (unguarded, fixed) and Series.ts:366 (getAllData, already guarded). Reproduced the exact TypeError before fixing. New test test/ut/spec/data/linkSeriesData.test.ts asserts (a) a plain line series: getData('node') does not throw and returns the main data, getAllData() returns one entry, and (b) a graph series still resolves getData('edge') and getAllData() with 2 entries, so linked behaviour is unchanged.

requirements.summary: The old `minmax` entry in the samplers map compared Math.abs(value) and emitted a single value per frame at the frame's MIDDLE index, so whenever a frame did not straddle zero the local minimum was never picked (troughs vanished) and the surviving point sat at the wrong position. Removed `minmax` from the samplers map (a Sampler can only return one value per frame) and added SeriesData#minmaxDownSample(valueDimension, rate), which walks each frame tracking both the min index and the max index by actual value, marks them (plus the frame's first NaN so null gaps are preserved) and materialises the result via `store.filter([], cb)` — indices are collected ascending, so both extrema are emitted in data order. dataSample.ts now dispatches `sampling === 'minmax'` to it, alongside the existing lttb branch. Also added 'minmaxDownSample' to TRANSFERABLE_METHODS and DOWNSAMPLE_METHODS so the pipeline's setOutputEnd/linked-data wrapping still applies (minmax emits ~2 points per frame).
requirements.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: upstream implements this as DataStore#minmaxDownSample, but src/data/DataStore.ts is outside my cluster scope, so I built the equivalent inside SeriesData.ts on top of the public DataStore#filter (which clones sharing chunks, keeps a subset of raw indices in ascending data order and clears the extent cache) — the resulting index set and order are identical to the upstream algorithm. If you want byte-level parity with upstream, the loop in SeriesData#minmaxDownSample should be moved into DataStore#minmaxDownSample. Other samplers (average, sum, max, min, nearest) and the lttb branch are untouched. Test test/ut/spec/data/minmaxDownSample.test.ts has 7 cases including all-positive and all-negative frames (which the old abs-based code got wrong), flat/short frames, null gaps, non-mutation of the source, and an end-to-end 2000-point line with sampling:'minmax' asserting the sampled extent equals the raw extent. I verified the old algorithm yields min 34.34 vs raw 30.00 on that dataset, so the e2e test genuinely discriminates.
